prediction_scored: miss. E = 0.182% (-0.785 to 1.159). refute_if (upper bound below +1.5%) is met, by 0.34 points, less than one standard error (0.50 points), so within sampling error (rule 10). support_if is not met. A detour of 1.5% (about 0.02 miles, 100 feet, per trip) is excluded under the registered estimator; one of up to 1.2% is not.
settle: The registered estimator nets out the year-over-year change of the preceding summer. That summer (July to September 2019) already showed a rise in the treated pairs' distance (+1.3%, +0.8%, +0.6% against a year earlier), when the M14 SBS began and the busway's August start was stopped by a court order. If drivers changed routes in that summer, the netting removes part of the effect. Route-level data (which street a trip used) would settle it.

research_needed.question: Did traffic volume on 14th Street fall by more than it rose on 12th, 13th and 15th to 18th Streets (evaporation)?
research_needed.data: Automated or manual counts on each crosstown street from 2nd to 10th Avenue for at least two months before and after; DOT's own ATR counts behind the Sam Schwartz reports are not in 7ym2-wayt (four 2019 locations only).
research_needed.design: Before-after with control streets in Midtown; publish the counts.

research_needed.question: Was the small rise in trip distance a detour caused by the busway or the continuation of a drift that began in 2018?
research_needed.data: TLC trip records with GPS traces (not public since mid-2016) or app-company route data; taxi zone pairs at finer scale.
research_needed.design: Route-level comparison of the share of crosstown trips using 14th Street before and after.

research_needed.question: Did the busway change injuries on 14th Street and its parallel streets, and NO2 along the corridor?
research_needed.data: h9gi-nx95 crashes by street segment; NYCCAS street-level monitors on 14th Street (if any) or low-cost sensors.
research_needed.design: Registered before-after with control corridors, segment-level counts.

research_needed.question: The System Public Graph holds no finding on road-space reallocation, traffic evaporation or displaced traffic.
research_needed.data: Transport literature (Cairns et al. 1998, 2002; Nello-Deakin 2022; bus-lane evaluations) is outside the graph's health-centred corpus.
research_needed.design: Add transport-research studies with travel-time and volume outcomes.

notes: Secondary estimates, not deciding: all busway hours 0.948% (0.06 to 1.844); overnight 0.189% (-0.741 to 1.127). The plain year-over-year DiD on weekdays gives 1.243% (0.745 to 1.743), against +0.59% (0.14 to 1.04) for the same estimator in the placebo year, so about half of it is drift that predates the busway. Exploratory: every one of the five post-busway months shows a year-over-year rise in the contrast (+0.8% to +1.4%, rising month by month), against a pre-busway monthly standard deviation of 0.7%; a detour of about 0.5% to 1% (35 to 65 feet per trip) is the most likely size, and the registered test cannot separate it from drift. Exploratory, evaporation of taxi demand: weekday trip counts in the treated pairs relative to control changed by -0.59% on the same summer-netted estimator (placebo seasons 1.55% and 2.26%, monthly sd 3.41%), so taxi demand in the corridor did not visibly fall. Weekday daytime trips between the treated zones averaged 11.52 minutes and 1.257 miles in October 2018 to February 2019 (128,579 trips) and 11.41 minutes and 1.289 miles in October 2019 to February 2020 (102,600 trips). Control-group sensitivity of the weekday estimate (exploratory): against Midtown pairs only, duration -0.2% (-4.22 to 3.97) and distance -0.12%; against downtown pairs only, duration 2.53% (-1.21 to 6.42) and distance 0.6% (-0.82 to 2.04). The registered estimator has no resampling, so rule 9 does not apply. Placebo seasons 2017 and 2018 were recomputed with the post months included and are unchanged.
notes_referee: Referee reproduced +0.18% (-0.79 to +1.16). Verdict stands. The summer 2019 baseline was already high; other baselines give +0.2% to +1.2%. Yellow-taxi trips in these pairs fell 20%, so composition may move distance.
